chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Al-Husayn Al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah Al-Barqi, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman, from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad Al-Sayqal. He was a Kufan, a freed servant (mawla), and his kunya was Abu Al-Walid.

key_terms.السَّعْدَآبَادِيِّ: Al-Sa'dabadi, a nisba indicating origin or residence
key_terms.الصِّيقِلِ: Al-Sayqal, meaning the goldsmith, a laqab (nickname) for Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ: Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, a prominent narrator
key_terms.كُنْيَتُهُ: His kunya, a teknonym used as an honorific
key_terms.مَوْلًى: Mawla, a freed servant or client

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies Shaykh al-Saduq’s rigorous methodology in *Al-Faqih*, where he meticulously traces the *isnad* to establish the reliability of narrations from Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal. By detailing the specific chain from himself back to the Kufi mawla Abu al-Walid, al-Saduq underscores the importance of verified transmission lines in preserving the authenticity of Imami jurisprudence and hadith.
